verified.claim: Per-partner fund-health data is not publicly available
verified.proof: NSFDC publishes the norms but not the per-partner figures. Searched NSFDC and socialjustice.gov.in; no partner-wise NPA report exists publicly. All partners carry status UNKNOWN. NOTE: the norms are partner-type-specific — RRB net NPA below 15% in 3 of 6 years (general allocation) vs below 10% (Stand-up India) vs NBFC-MFI below 0.5%. An earlier version of this entry recorded a single '10%' threshold, which was the Stand-up India rule misread as the general one.

verified.claim: All encoded partner prudential norms match NSFDC's own wording verbatim
verified.proof: Fetched three Wayback captures of the original NSFDC pages and diffed against eligibilityNorms.ts. Confirmed exactly: RRB 'Net NPA must be less than 15% in at least 3 years out of last 6 years'; RRB profit 'at least in 3 out of last 6 financial years'; release norms '(a) Government/Bank Guarantee (b) no overdues more than one year old (c) minimum 80% cumulative utilization'; PSB 'Utilisation Certificate for interest switch over ... no overdues payable at the time of disbursement'; NBFC-MFI 'Gross NPA less than 2% and net NPA below 0.5%', 'mfr5 by CRISIL', '3 years of continuous profit track record'.

verified.claim: The voice pipeline works end to end from the text-query stage onward
verified.proof: Typed a question into /voice in the browser: phase advanced idle -> thinking -> speaking, the answer rendered with its NSFDC citations, TTS fired, and the suggested action and follow-up chips appeared. Web Speech API constructor confirmed present (window.SpeechRecognition || window.webkitSpeechRecognition === true), so the mic path is live on web rather than stubbed.

verified.claim: The assistant stub was answering with pre-verification loan figures
verified.proof: Asked 'What interest rate will I pay?' on the new voice screen and it read aloud 'micro-credit products sit around 5-6% per year' — Micro Finance is verified at 6.5% and Aajeevika at 15%, so the answer understated the dearest product by threefold. Also found 'Term Loan goes up to Rs 50 lakh' (that is the project cost; the loan cap is Rs 45 lakh), an education loan quoted at 'about 6%' and 'Rs 30 lakh in India' against a verified 6.5% and Rs 40 lakh, and OPEN_SCHEME/OPEN_PARTNER actions pointing at 'nsfdc-education-india' and 'sca-mh-001', neither of which exists any more. All figures now derived from MOCK_SCHEMES; re-tested and the answer reads 6.5%-15% with NSFDC citations.

verified.claim: Voice works on the chat screen and degrades exactly as ADR-010 requires
verified.proof: In the preview browser at /assistant: mic renders as 'Speak' alongside 'Send'. Mic access is blocked in the pane, and tapping it showed 'I need permission to use the microphone. You can type your question instead.' with the button resetting to 'Speak' rather than sticking. A TYPED question did not auto-speak (spied window.speechSynthesis.speak -> [] and the button still read 'Read aloud'); tapping 'Read aloud' then spoke and flipped it to 'Stop'. Forcing detectProvider() unavailable in source and reloading: the mic disappeared entirely while Send and the composer stayed usable, and /voice showed 'This browser cannot listen to speech. Try Chrome, or type your question below.' Source restored, git diff clean.

verified.proof: Audited all nine routes in src/api/endpoints.ts. Six consumed endpoints each have a service function and a section in docs/API_CONTRACT.md; assistant.stream and assistant.transcribe are documented and contracted but deliberately not consumed. grep for "from '@/api/mock" across app/, src/components/, src/hooks/ -> clean. grep for fetch( outside src/api/client.ts -> clean.

verified.claim: Flipping EXPO_PUBLIC_USE_MOCK_API=false produces a working bundle, but the mock DATA still ships
verified.proof: EXPO_PUBLIC_USE_MOCK_API=false EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=https://api.example.com npx expo export --platform android -> exit 0. Grepping the resulting Hermes bundle still finds MPBCDC, TAHDCO, Aajeevika, sca-mh-mpbcdc and nsfdc-term-loan, because every service statically imports @/api/mock/server and USE_MOCK_API is a runtime branch Metro cannot drop. Behaviour is correct — requests do go to the API — so this is a bundle-size characteristic, documented in BACKEND_HANDOFF § What still ships in backend mode, not a bug.

verified.claim: Marathi has no text-to-speech voice on macOS, and asking for one fails silently
verified.proof: speechSynthesis.getVoices() in the preview browser (180 voices): en-IN Rishi, hi-IN Lekha, bn-IN Piya, ta-IN Vani, te-IN Geeta all present; mr-IN returned ZERO, including base-language matches. verified.claim: Every speech-to-text error kind renders its own actionable message

openQuestions: Which languages beyond these six does the jury expect? The i18n layer takes a new one in about 15 minutes.
Will the backend serve the scheme catalogue, or does it stay bundled for offline use? (Recommendation: serve it, cache aggressively — the client already caches for an hour.)
Is there a real data source for partner NPA / fund-utilisation, or is that figure modelled for the demo?

AMY income ceiling: the archived NSFDC AMY page (2025-02-15 capture) reads 'Annual Family Income of applicants should be below Rs. 30.00 lakhs for both rural and urban areas'. Our catalogue applies the general ₹5.00 lakh ceiling to AMY. ₹30 lakh is 6x the ceiling we verified twice (NSFDC + socialjustice.gov.in, effective 07.01.2026), is implausible for an SC micro-finance product, and reads like a decimal slip for 'Rs. 3.00 lakh' — which was the pre-2026 general ceiling, consistent with a capture that predates the change. NOT changed: relaxing a hard eligibility gate on an ambiguous figure would wrongly admit applicants, and tightening it wrongly excludes them. Needs a current official page or a circular to settle. See src/api/mock/fixtures/schemes.ts (nsfdc-amy).

Endpoint naming: the backend teammate's pipeline diagram calls the chat stage '/v1/chat'; this repo's contract has always called it 'POST /v1/assistant/query' (docs/API_CONTRACT.md). Same endpoint, two names. Settle it in the contract rather than aliasing in the client.

Which speech-to-text languages actually work? The Web Speech API does not expose a supported-language list, so this cannot be enumerated in code — it needs a human speaking each of the six into a real device. Chrome delegates to Google's engine (which documents all six Indian locales); Safari uses Apple's, with different coverage. Untested as of 2026-09-08.
